source_evidence: If a stable NAV money market fund’s NAV per share deviates by more than half a cent from $1.00, the fund must re-price its shares to something other than $1.00.
answer: Breaking the buck refers to a stable-NAV money market fund having to reprice its shares below or above the usual $1.00 when its NAV per share deviates from $1.00 by more than half a cent. If this happens, an investor’s holding in the fund loses value. The source notes that this is rare, but it can happen when the fund faces substantial losses on some of its holdings.
